subject: Food Science
title: Carbonation and Fizz
description: A quick, practical guide to Carbonation and Fizz.

hook.text: The tingle of sparkling water isn't from the bubbles popping—it's from carbonic acid stimulating pain and sour receptors on your.

buildup.text: CO₂ dissolves in water to form carbonic acid. The acid, not the physical bubbles, creates the biting sensation you feel in.

discovery.text: An enzyme called carbonic anhydrase on your tongue converts dissolved CO₂ to acid in real time.

twist.text: Altitude affects carbonation perception. At high elevations, lower air pressure allows CO₂ to escape faster.

climax.text: Champagne has about 49 million bubbles per glass—each one releasing aroma compounds as it bursts at the surface, enhancing flavor.

punchline.text: Fizz is chemistry, not physics. The tingle is acid, not bubbles.

quiz.question: What actually causes the tingling sensation in carbonated drinks?
options: Carbonic acid stimulating pain and sour receptors on the tongue
